sections.title: Introduction
body: An Array is a linear data structure that stores elements of the same data type in contiguous memory locations.
Each element can be accessed directly using its index.
Arrays provide fast access to elements using index-based addressing.
They are one of the most fundamental data structures used in programming.

sections.title: Properties
body: Stores elements of homogeneous data type.
Elements are stored in contiguous memory locations.
Each element is accessed using an index (starting from 0 in most languages).
Array size is fixed at the time of creation (in static arrays).

sections.title: Operations
body: Access:
- Directly access any element using its index.
Insertion:
- Insert element at a specific position.
- Shift elements to the right if required.
Deletion:
- Delete element from a specific position.
- Shift elements to the left to fill the gap.
Traversal:
- Visit each element of the array sequentially.
Searching:
- Linear Search: Check each element one by one.
- Binary Search: Works only on sorted arrays.

sections.title: Types of Arrays
body: One-Dimensional Array: Stores elements in a single row.
Two-Dimensional Array: Stores elements in rows and columns (matrix form).
Multi-Dimensional Array: Arrays with more than two dimensions.
Dynamic Array: Size can be changed at runtime (e.g., Vector in C++, ArrayList in Java).

sections.title: Applications
body: Used to store and manage collections of data.
Used in sorting and searching algorithms.
Used to represent matrices and tables.
Used in implementing other data structures like stacks, queues, and heaps.

sections.title: Advantages
body: Fast access to elements using index (O(1)).
Efficient memory utilization due to contiguous allocation.
Easy to implement and use.
Suitable for storing large amounts of data of the same type.

sections.title: Disadvantages
body: Fixed size (in static arrays) leads to memory wastage or overflow.
Insertion and deletion operations are costly due to shifting.
Cannot store different data types together.
Requires contiguous memory block.

sections.title: Time Complexity
body: Access:
Search:
- Linear Search: O(n)
- Binary Search: O(log n)
Insertion:
- Best Case: O(1)
- Worst Case: O(n)
Deletion:
- Best Case: O(1)
- Worst Case: O(n)
